points.title: Array and 2D array
points.must: Definitions: array = fixed number of elements of one type under one identifier, accessed by index; 2D array = array of arrays in rows and columns, two indexes [row][column].
points.model:
Array = data structure storing a fixed number of elements of the same data type under one identifier; each element accessed by its index.
2D array = array of arrays: elements in rows and columns like a table; each element accessed with two indexes [row][column].

points.title: Why a 2D array instead of several 1D arrays
points.must: One identifier, loops can reach all elements by changing indexes; separate arrays cannot be looped over.
points.model: marks1, marks2, marks3 = separate identifiers: the code must be repeated and a loop cannot move from one to the next. A 2D array keeps all 12 marks under one name and nested loops reach every element by changing the indexes.

points.title: Terms
points.must: Identifier, element, index, row, column, dimension, lower bound, upper bound, size, with values for the marks array.
points.model:
marks = [[7,8,6,9],[10,9,9,8],[5,6,7,6]] (3 pupils × 4 tests).
Identifier marks; element = one value; index [1][2] → 9; first index = row, second = column; dimension 2; lower bound 0 (pseudocode often 1); upper bound rows 2, columns 3; size 3 × 4 = 12.
Number of elements in a dimension = upper − lower + 1. Index outside the bounds → error.

points.title: Uses of 2D arrays
points.must: Examples of data with two coordinates: images, spreadsheets, timetables, game boards, distance tables.
points.model: Image pixels image[row][col]; spreadsheet cells; timetable[day][lesson]; chess 8×8, noughts and crosses 3×3; distance table dist[i][j] between cities.

points.title: Accessing an element
points.must: marks[2] = whole row (1D array), then [1] picks the element; assigning; jagged arrays use count($a[$r]).
points.model: marks[2] = [5, 6, 7, 6] (a 1D array); marks[2][1] = 6. $marks[2][1] = 8; changes only that element. Jagged array = rows of different lengths → inner loop uses count($a[$r]).

points.title: Declaring and initialising
points.must: Pseudocode DECLARE … ARRAY[1:3, 1:4] OF INTEGER; PHP/Python/JS list of lists; same element with different bases; zero-filled array with nested loops; Python trap.

points.title: Cinema seating example
points.must: seats[5][8] of 'F'/'B', 40 elements; convert seat numbers to indexes with −1; check bounds before use.
points.model: 5 rows × 8 seats → $seats[5][8], 40 elements. Row 3 seat 5 → $seats[2][4]; if ($seats[2][4] == "F") $seats[2][4] = "B"; else "Seat taken". Check 0 ≤ r ≤ 4 and 0 ≤ c ≤ 7 first.

points.title: Nested loop
points.must: Definition; outer = rows, inner = columns; inner body runs rows × columns times; row-by-row visiting order.
points.model:
Nested loop = a loop inside another loop; for each outer iteration the inner loop runs all its iterations → inner body runs outer × inner times (3 × 4 = 12).
for r ← 0 to 2 (rows) / for c ← 0 to 3 (columns) / visit a[r][c]. Order: [0][0], [0][1] … [0][3], [1][0] …

points.title: Row totals
points.must: Code with $sum = 0 inside the outer loop; results 30, 36, 24.
points.model:
for ($r = 0; $r < count($marks); $r++) { $sum = 0; for ($c = 0; $c < count($marks[$r]); $c++) { $sum += $marks[$r][$c]; } echo $sum / count($marks[$r]); }
Totals 30, 36, 24; averages 7.5, 9, 6. Reset inside the outer loop or totals keep growing.

points.title: Column totals
points.must: Swap the loops: outer over columns count($marks[0]), inner over rows; results 22, 23, 22, 23; pseudocode with grand total 90.
points.model:
for ($c = 0; $c < count($marks[0]); $c++) { $sum = 0; for ($r = 0; $r < count($marks); $r++) $sum += $marks[$r][$c]; echo $sum; } → 22, 23, 22, 23.
Pseudocode: FOR Row ← 1 TO 3 / Total ← 0 / FOR Col ← 1 TO 4 / Total ← Total + Marks[Row, Col] / NEXT Col … Grand total 90.

points.title: Steps to write 2D-array code
points.must: Meaning of rows/columns → loop order → where to initialise → inner-body action → where to output → check bounds and trace.
points.model: 1) What rows/columns mean and bounds. 2) Per row → outer over rows; per column → outer over columns. 3) Whole-array result: initialise before both loops; per row/column: inside the outer loop. 4) One action in the inner body. 5) Output after inner loop (per row) or after both. 6) Check bounds, trace.

points.title: Standard algorithms
points.must: Grand total, count, maximum with position (start at first element), linear search with stopping early, one row/column/diagonal with a single loop.
points.model: Total 90; count marks ≥ 8 → 6; max: $max = $a[0][0]; if ($a[$r][$c] > $max) {$max=…; $mr=$r; $mc=$c;} → 10 at [1][0] (pupil 2, test 1); start at first element so negatives work. Search: flag Found, stop early (break 2 / WHILE NOT Found). One row: fix the row index; one column: fix the column index; diagonal $a[$i][$i].

points.title: Choosing 1D or 2D
points.must: One value per item → 1D; several values of the same type / grid → 2D; different types → records / associative arrays; justification names size, type, meaning of rows and columns, processing.
points.model:
Names of 25 pupils → 1D [25]. Marks of 30 pupils in 5 tests → 2D [30][5]. Cinema 12×20, board 3×3, shop × day sales → 2D. Name, grade, birth date → array of records / associative arrays (or 2D of strings).
Good justification: 'A 2D array of integers, 30 rows (pupils) × 6 columns (tests), because each pupil has six marks of the same type and totals per pupil and per test are needed.' Parallel arrays are harder to keep in step.

points.title: Database rows in a 2D array
points.must: while ($row = mysqli_fetch_row($result)) $students[] = $row; row = record, column = field in SELECT order; fetch_all; associative rows; reasons.
points.model:
$students = []; while ($row = mysqli_fetch_row($result)) { $students[] = $row; }
$students[0][0] = "Aruzhan", $students[4][2] = "Shymkent", count($students) = 5 rows, count($students[0]) = 3 columns. fetch_all($result, MYSQLI_ASSOC) → $rows[2]["City"]. Lets the program use the rows several times (display, totals, sort with usort) without running the query again.
